standard_prerequisites.name: Sections of a sheafification
standard_prerequisites.use: Describes the sections of a sheafification by coverings and local sections, which is the tool used in both directions.

core_obligations: Surjectivity (proof lines 2408-2425): given a section of the sheafification of the target over an object, the description of sections of a sheafification produces a covering and local sections of the target; the covering may be refined by objects on which the map of presheaves is bijective, where the local sections can be lifted, and the sheaf condition assembles the lifts.

Injectivity (proof lines 2427-2443): two local sections of the sheafification of the source with the same image are compared after refining so that both come from the source and the map is bijective there, and the sheaf condition on the target, together with the refinement by objects where the map is bijective, gives their equality.
proof_roadmap: Show surjectivity on sections by refining a covering to objects where the map is bijective and lifting locally.
Show injectivity similarly by comparing two sections after refinement.
Conclude that the map of sheafifications is an isomorphism.
difficulty_reason: The lemma states that a map of presheaves of sets whose components are bijective on a set of objects that covers every object becomes an isomorphism after sheafification (statement lines 2398-2405). The proof is a complete argument in two parts: surjectivity is proved by describing sections of a sheafification through a covering, refining that covering by objects where the map is bijective, lifting the local sections and assembling them by the sheaf condition (proof lines 2408-2425); injectivity is proved by refining so that two sections with the same image both come from the source and the map is bijective there (proof lines 2427-2443). The non-formal content is the two refinements and the use of the sheaf condition. The claim is H2: two written-out verifications with the covering input used explicitly.
